findings.reason: the unidentified second path is exactly what decides whether the fix's write paths are the right ones, so the plan should carry a done-when case that requires the two paths to be named (in the manifest and in the run's verdict record) before the code cases count.
findings.text: `s22`'s deliverable part 1 ("Find the paths first. From the run's records, name the code paths that made the two attempts. Record them in the manifest before changing code") is the plan's own statement that the cause is not yet known — its Why says "the verdict log holds no row for the request, so which two paths attempted the launch is not yet known" — yet no done-when case measures it, so a node can land both code fixes, pass all four cases, and never have determined whether the second attempt came through `_launch_queued`/`_stamp_failure` at all; if it did not, the two fixes are repairing a path that is not the one that lost the fields.

findings.reason: the claim is either narrowed to the covered path or the dispatch-gate read must be brought inside the per-pass record, and until one is chosen a node can satisfy every case while the reads the section exists to remove survive on the fallback.
findings.text: `s4` concludes "so a pass reads each plan once however many requests name it", but `_plan_review_owed` returns to `_dispatch_gate_owed` for every request whose pointer records no current contract and for every request whose units no stored review covers (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3315`, :3325), and that fallback calls `routing.require_plan_reviewed`, which itself runs `plan_review.review_coverage`, `read_plan_review`, `_plan_html.read_state_file` and `list_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2704–2741`) — per request, outside the per-pass record; done-when case 1 only counts the covered path, so the section's central claim and its gate disagree on precisely the unreviewed-plan case the reported 1,250–2,980 s launch stage would still be paying for.

findings.reason: the implementer will write the case on a lane-full pass, which does compute an order, so the code is unchanged; only the sentence overstates, and narrowing it to "each pass that computes an admission order" is a one-word edit.
findings.text: `s21`'s deliverable says "Each pass writes the request's queue position, rank key and last attempt verdict onto its pointer", but a pass whose gate is waiting (`local_gated`) records gated verdicts and then filters the queued list to nothing (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3665`, :3709–3735), so no order is computed and no position exists to write; done-when case 4 is worded "after a pass that launches nothing", which a gated pass satisfies while writing nothing, so the claim and its case describe different passes.
